review_kind: Source-contract review; not a formal proof of conformance to upstream prose or an independent human review.
scope: All 218 active stdSig/globalsSig predicate names, all published builtin/function entries, five explicitly excluded globals, and declaration/model rules. Unlisted global names are unsupported, not implicitly covered.

status_definitions.reviewed: Source comparison found no discrepancy for well-typed, defined inputs within the stated fragment; not a kernel-checked upstream equivalence theorem.
status_definitions.restricted: Agreement requires additional explicit premises not globally guaranteed by the interface.
status_definitions.extension: Project-specific spelling or a signature extension; not strict native ABI conformance.
status_definitions.nonconformant: A concrete signature/semantic discrepancy or an unestablished representation contract remains; linked findings prevent a clean conformance gate.
status_definitions.unsupported: No implementation signature or explicitly excluded input family.

findings.title: Graph ABI mismatch
findings.problem: N/E parameters are omitted; root/source/sink parameter positions differ from the pinned native predicates. Steiner decoding discards a root and WST invents a node count from endpoints/edge count.
findings.repair: Registered both pinned overloads for every overloaded graph predicate and dispatch on arity. The decoder now follows the upstream order exactly (N,E before the arrays only in _int forms; root/source/sink before ns,es), uses 1..N / 1..E without inferring counts from endpoints, keeps steiner existential and dsteiner/dwst rooted, and restricts wst/dwst to their declared from/to/es length.

findings.title: Automaton final-state ABI and state validation
findings.problem: F is an integer indicator array here, but the pinned signature requires a set. Q upper bounds are not enforced during transitions. NFA frontier fold can drop earlier accumulated successors.
findings.repair: Decode F as a set of int; enforce 1..Q on q0, every intermediate/final state and every d target (nonempty words), and 1..S on symbols; make the NFA frontier the union of all successor sets; empty words check only q0 in F (cost: total_cost = 0); decoders reject Q < 0, S < 0 and flat matrix lengths different from Q*S (restricted).

findings.title: Matrix representation lacks a source contract
findings.problem: Signatures flatten native multidimensional arguments without a proved flattening ABI. LexChain/diffn_k decoders instead require nested Value.array, which cannot pass their flat integer-array signature.
findings.repair: Adopted an explicit FlatZinc 1-D array ABI. fzn_table_int recovers the column count C=length(xs) and rejects empty/nondivisible tables; fzn_geost* recover C=k, gate length(xs) >= k*length(kind) and (for bb) the bound lengths, and are restricted to the upstream shape-index fragment. fzn_lex_chain_*, fzn_lex2, fzn_strict_lex2 and fzn_lex_chain_lesseq_orbitope have no recoverable matrix width; fzn_diffn_k/fzn_diffn_nonstrict_k have no recoverable box dimension count. Those forms reject flat calls as unsupported. Witnesses cover an accepted flat table call, accepted restricted geost calls, length mismatches, and every unsupported rejection.

findings.title: Unvalidated shape and partiality premises
findings.problem: Several mathematical helpers use zip, getD or unchecked parallel lengths; others impose equal lengths where a raw native relation can have a larger unused parallel array. Their result can differ from the upstream partial relation on malformed or mismatched data; static element types alone do not enforce the required shapes or public-library admissibility premises. Packing also needs its documented nonnegative weights/capacity domain: native bin ranges include unoccupied bins, while the local scalar-capacity helper checks occupied bins only.
findings.repair: Replaced the silent zip/getD/[i]! shape and index defaults with per-read three-valued gates: a read is required only when the upstream evaluation reaches it, an out-of-bounds int or set read makes the predicate false, and an out-of-bounds bool read uses MiniZinc's false value. Parallel-length, first-true, last-write, longer-unused-array and short-array cases are kernel-checked. Six residual rows (fzn_bin_packing, fzn_cost_mdd, fzn_cumulatives, fzn_cumulatives_decomp, fzn_global_cardinality_low_up_closed, fzn_mdd_nondet) carry explicit restricted preconditions.

findings.title: Graph relation omits node/endpoint constraints
findings.problem: Reachability/connectedness interpreters do not conjoin subgraph validity; DAG ignores node selection; directed tree edge count plus reachability does not alone enforce all endpoint rules. Path helper nests the sink constraint inside the source implication.
findings.repair: Replaced the handwritten graph algorithms with literal transcriptions of the pinned fzn_* decompositions: endpoint/subgraph constraints, DAG distances, selected-root and parent/distance conditions, tree edge counts, and separate path source/sink degree conjuncts. Auxiliary dist/parent/bridge arrays are existentials with the upstream declared ranges, and each Bool twin is proved equal to its Prop body.

findings.title: Deterministic/cost MDD semantics too weak
findings.problem: Interpreter searches for a first successful walk. The deterministic upstream MDD activates all matching edges and enforces one active node per level; the cost version includes additional active-edge constraints. A path-existence algorithm needs structural premises and an equivalence argument.
findings.repair: fzn_mdd is now a literal conjunction of the pinned deterministic MDD constraints (matching edges activate all matching transitions, one active node per level); fzn_cost_mdd is implemented exactly on the canonical one-node-per-level fragment and recorded restricted outside it; fzn_mdd_nondet remains a separate restricted existential walk search. The reviewer self-loop counterexample and deterministic/cost witnesses are kernel-checked regressions.

findings.title: Nonpositive sliding-window handling
findings.problem: windowsB returns true for all w <= 0. For w = 0 and nonempty xs, the pinned decomposition still checks low <= 0 <= up at each zero-width window. Negative widths lead to invalid prefix-array references, not automatic success. Reopened 2026-11-17: an empty xs was still accepted (w = 0 with low <= 0 <= up, and every w > 0), although min(index_set(xs)) in fzn_sliding_sum.mzn is undefined on an empty array, so upstream rejects every such call.
findings.repair: windowStarts (shared by windowsB and the three Props) is undefined, hence false, for an empty xs and for a negative width; otherwise it is the upstream generator 0..n-w: w = 0 checks low <= 0 <= up at each of the n+1 empty windows, and w > n is vacuous. Kernel-checked ABI regressions cover the eight mandatory sliding_sum witnesses (the empty-array one now false), an empty-array w > n witness, zero-width and empty-array witnesses for sliding_among_int and sliding_among_bool; the empty-array values were confirmed with MiniZinc 2.10.1 (Gecode -G std and Chuffed: 'minimum of empty set is undefined', UNSATISFIABLE).

findings.title: Coefficient indices silently dropped
findings.problem: sumPred helpers filter out nonexistent coefficient indices, whereas the pinned parameter sums index coefficients[k] directly. Example sets=[{2}], coefficients=[7], idx=1,total=0 is accepted locally.
findings.repair: coeffsAt? now returns none for an out-of-range coefficient index, both in the selected set and in every other set (the upstream sums comprehension is evaluated for every j). The predicate is then false; the all-defined case sums coefficients after extensional set deduplication. Kernel-checked witnesses cover the selected set, another set, the accepted case and an empty unselected set.

findings.title: Cumulative differs on empty inputs and negative resources
findings.problem: Local universal time relation requires capacity >= 0 even for no tasks; pinned fzn_cumulative returns true for an empty task array. Local accumulation includes negative resources; pinned Tasks excludes resources whose upper bound is nonpositive.
findings.repair: cumulativeProp/B now enforce the cumulative.mzn wrapper contract: the three arrays share an index set and all durations and resources are nonnegative. Tasks are selected by duration > 0 and resource > 0; with no selected task the result is true iff length(start) = 0 or capacity >= 0; otherwise usage is checked at every time. Kernel-checked empty, negative-resource, overlap and disjoint regressions; the row is restricted to the wrapper contract.

findings.title: Duplicate cover behavior differs from raw decomposition
findings.problem: Local gcc omits the pinned implied length(xs) >= sum(count). For xs=[1],cover=[1,1],count=[1,1], the local relation is true but raw fzn_global_cardinality is false. Distinct-cover assumptions cannot be silently applied to arbitrary FlatZinc text.
findings.repair: gccProp/B now conjoin the implied length(xs) >= sum(count) over all count entries and make a count shorter than cover false. Duplicate cover values are no longer assumed distinct. Kernel-checked duplicate-cover, short-count and open/closed regressions; the SC-04 shape gate is closed for fzn_global_cardinality and fzn_global_cardinality_closed.

findings.title: Negative task durations accepted
findings.problem: Singleton negative-duration tasks bypassed pairwise overlap checks. Both pinned disjunctive decompositions explicitly require nonnegative durations.
findings.repair: Added duration nonnegativity to Prop and Bool definitions and kernel-checked negative/zero-duration regressions.

findings.title: Task index used instead of machine index
findings.problem: cumulatives looked up bound[j] for task j and discarded min_machine; unrelated machines could accept or reject incorrectly.
findings.repair: Bounds now use the assigned machine; native ids are normalized by min_machine. Kernel-checked upper/lower/asymmetric/offset/empty regressions. The cumulatives parallel-length restriction remains recorded under SC-04; the machine-bound repair itself is exact.

findings.title: All-false conditional partiality was overconstrained
findings.problem: With no true condition, upstream implications impose no restriction on b. The old helper forced b=false.
findings.repair: Both Prop and Bool now leave b unrestricted; kernel-checked all-false and first-true regressions.

findings.title: Knapsack omitted nonnegativity guards
findings.problem: The raw upstream native predicate requires nonnegative item counts and nonnegative total weight/profit. The old relation checked only the dot products.
findings.repair: Added all three guards to Prop and Bool; kernel-checked negative-count/negative-total and positive regressions.

findings.title: Set enumeration duplicates counted as distinct members
findings.problem: at_most1 counted duplicate enumeration entries as multiple intersection elements; sum_pred could add one coefficient repeatedly for a duplicated set index. Both disagree with extensional set semantics.
findings.repair: Deduplicate shared intersection elements and sum_pred set indices; kernel-checked acceptance/rejection regressions. The out-of-range-index issue remains SC-08.

model_rules.contract: One ordered sequence of predicate, parameter, variable, constraint items and one solve item; full consumption.
model_rules.notes: The independent character-level Lexes relation and GrModel are composed by the unconditional Lexical.parseModel_iff_sourceGrammar theorem. Lexer soundness/completeness are proved for the declared non-float/R11 policy; equivalence of every chosen convention to upstream syntax remains a separate review/proof obligation.

model_rules.contract: Unique predicate names, formal argument names, and a shared unique parameter/variable namespace.
model_rules.notes: Names and expression types are statically checked; runtime checker does not trust user-declared predicate meanings.

model_rules.contract: Parameters are fixed by literal declarations and cannot be reassigned by a solution.
model_rules.notes: Satisfies alone omits this condition. Certification statements about instances must use Satisfies AND ParamHonest, or IsSolution.

model_rules.contract: Finite ranges are closed; set equality is extensional and duplicates do not change membership/cardinality.
model_rules.notes: Reversed ranges denote empty sets; explicit empty-domain inputs can be unsupported by search without a false verdict.

model_rules.contract: All variable domain restrictions and initializer equalities hold simultaneously.
model_rules.notes: Forward references and alias cycles use the documented global-environment policy R5/R6; inconsistent initializers are unsatisfiable, not overwritten.

model_rules.contract: Arrays are flat, 1-based, have declared lengths and correctly typed elements.
model_rules.notes: Syntax.IndexSet represents only 1..hi; WellFormed enforces declaration lengths and element typing. Cross-argument premises for all 13 restricted predicates are explicitly gated or excluded by Semantics.Admission; normalized flat matrix ABIs remain a declared subset, not an inferred upstream lowering theorem.

model_rules.contract: Satisfaction requires all constraints, domains and initializers; optimization additionally attains an objective and compares all parameter-honest solutions.
model_rules.notes: Integer objective only; supported solver objective shapes are narrower than typed AST objectives. Completion is required for optimality.

model_rules.contract: Search annotations may affect strategy but cannot alter satisfying assignments.
model_rules.notes: Annotation grammar extensions R28 and escape rules R11 are documented. Verify strategy soundness separately from semantic interpretation.

model_rules.contract: Use exact mathematical integers and finite integer sets.
model_rules.notes: A1 explicitly chooses unbounded Lean Int. Machine-specific integer limits must be separate checks; floats/optional values are excluded.

model_rules.contract: Checker solutions assign declared variables once; omissions may be completed from evaluable declaration initializers.
model_rules.notes: A7/A10 is a checker-interface policy, not a FlatZinc model-semantics ambiguity; projected output without an initializer extension can be rejected.

model_rules.contract: The documented language admits scalar parameters and selected annotation/index spelling extensions.
model_rules.notes: These policies must remain distinguishable from exact BNF conformance; they are not evidence that MiniZinc translation is certified.

model_rules.contract: Registered native predicate names may be resolved from the external signature table without a model declaration.
model_rules.notes: The FlatZinc prose requires nonstandard predicate declarations. Accepting undeclared registered names is a project interface extension, not exact context-sensitive input conformance. Declared signatures take precedence for typing; dynamic meaning still comes from the fixed name table, not a user predicate body.
